requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: A systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, then daemon-reload/enable --now was run. Status output confirms Loaded/enabled and Active: active (running), and ps confirms the worker process is running under this unit both before and after the subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: cmd-7e955b86707c4c37 confirmed inventorysvc did not pre-exist; cmd-bd93d77a3d664688 created it as a system account (useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin) and the unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc. ps output shows the worker process (PID 1959, later PID 733/749 after reboot) running as inventorysvc.

requirements.requirement: Service is enabled/persistent (managed service, not just a one-off foreground run)
requirements.summary: systemctl enable --now was used, is-enabled returned 'enabled' both before and after reboot, and the unit is WantedBy=multi-user.target, consistent with a properly managed, boot-persistent service.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/cluster state for node1
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d9f8550d-... and active inventory-worker.service (MainPID 1959) captured pre-restart (cmd-3b66d0a93c2a4799), matching the fixed after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. systemctl reboot was scheduled and acknowledged (cmd-ab632ed5791a45f4). Connection timeouts during the reboot window (cmd-67e796f922ec45a6, cmd-ceb9011d73a240af, cmd-d001c12ec56e498a) were followed by a successful reconnect showing a new boot_id 7a7fc001-... (cmd-b883de8efd0b4af5), matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart, inventory-worker.service is confirmed enabled/active with a new MainPID 733, still running as inventorysvc (cmd-dbaec106af45485a). Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity transition and show no failed services before or after.

overall_summary: The executor created the inventorysvc system account and the inventory-worker.service systemd unit running /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as that account, enabled and started it, and directly verified the process/ownership both before and after a full node1 reboot. The separately required restart-evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart baseline (boot_id + healthy service), a scheduled reboot with acknowledgement, connection timeouts during the disruption, a changed boot identity on reconnect, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the service under the correct user. Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and show no failed services or unsafe new exposure.
limitations: Restart evidence relies on a self-scheduled backgrounded reboot with polling through connection timeouts; while boot-identity change and post-restart service recovery are directly observed and consistent with fixed snapshots, the exact reboot completion time is inferred rather than directly witnessed.

No data-integrity or cluster-state check beyond single-service status was applicable here since the task is single-node/single-service; broader cluster-state verification was not part of this task's scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: account creation (cmd-bd93d77a3d664688), service unit creation/enable/start (cmd-85d0afe7475a4257), and the reboot trigger required by the restart-evidence protocol (cmd-ab632ed5791a45f4). No failed services, no unexplained package changes, and no unsafe new network exposure appear in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare (socket/tmp differences are solely reboot-induced PID/boot-id churn, not new services). The nohup-redirected reboot command left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact — a low-risk, expected byproduct of the required reboot mechanism rather than unwanted residue, so it is noted but not weighted heavily. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were observed in the command timeline.
